claims.statement: Verified example: Fronius warranty terms can require a commissioning protocol, invoice with serial number, rating-plate photo, and additional defect information before Fronius decides the warranty service.
Verified example: SolarEdge publishes a labor-reimbursement workflow for approved RMA replacements that requires an invoice and follows remote diagnosis and RMA approval.
Hypothesis (unvalidated): a distributor or second-tier OEM will pay for a neutral multi-brand workflow and permit enough data reuse to create a claims benchmark.

contrary_evidence: Fronius already runs serial-based registration, certificates, and installer-mediated claims, showing that OEM portals can own the workflow: https://www.fronius.com/en-us/usa/solar-energy/home-owners/products-and-solutions/warranties

SolarEdge already defines remote diagnosis, RMA approval, and labor reimbursement, so a neutral layer needs OEM authorization rather than merely digitizing public rules: https://www.solaredge.com/sites/default/files/warranty%20reimbursement%20%28updated%20March%202022%29.pdf

economics.acquisition_route: Build a quantified claim-journey dossier from installers, then sell a 90-day white-label pilot to one regional distributor rather than acquiring installers one by one.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Unvalidated scenario: 2 networks at PLN 15,000 MRR in year 2, 10 at PLN 22,000 MRR in year 4, and 18 at PLN 25,000 MRR in year 6 imply PLN 5.4m ARR before per-claim revenue. At 3-5x network-software value and 55% ownership, PLN 5m founder net worth is plausible in years 5-7; inability to secure one OEM/distributor design partner within 18 months invalidates the network path.
economics.founder_time: 4-5 hours/day through one network pilot; use a contract field-service specialist and do not promise 24/7 claim handling.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Hypothesis: 65-82%; manual technical adjudication and multilingual installer support are major costs and should be limited or partner-delivered.
economics.payback: Unvalidated customer hypothesis: fewer incomplete claims, lower handling time, and better reserve visibility repay implementation within 9-12 months; establish against the buyer's baseline.
economics.pricing: Unvalidated estimate: PLN 8,000-30,000 monthly per OEM/distributor network plus PLN 30-150 per closed claim; paid implementation for rule mapping.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Installed fleets generate claims for years; warranty rules, serial mappings, and service histories deeply embed the platform.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: permissioned cross-case defect, evidence, parts, and resolution data improve triage and reserve estimates; installer adoption creates a two-sided workflow moat
fingerprint.customer: PV, inverter, battery, and heat-pump OEMs or distributors with fragmented installer service networks in Central Europe
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: use the family renewables firm to document multi-brand friction, then approach one distributor or second-tier OEM with a bounded white-label pilot
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: white-label installer portal, rules engine, evidence completeness, telemetry attachments, RMA and shipment state, labor-invoice matching, and service analytics
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: OEM or distributor pays a platform fee and per claim when a case reaches an agreed disposition and reimbursement state
fingerprint.problem_trigger: a field failure creates a warranty claim that crosses installer diagnosis, OEM approval, replacement logistics, labor evidence, and reimbursement

founder_fit: The parents' installation company offers direct understanding of installer-side claim evidence without inventing customer commitments.
AI document extraction and failure classification suit the founder's data skills.
The model can scale through distributor/OEM networks rather than personal content.
A software-administration role avoids inventory-heavy hardware operations.
risks: OEMs may see claim data and adjudication as strategically sensitive.
Hardware diagnosis errors can create safety, liability, and customer-service harm.
Enterprise sales cycles may be long for a part-time founder.
Cross-brand benchmarking needs strict permissions and competition-law safeguards.

structure.control_point: complete claim case linking device entitlement, defect evidence, RMA disposition, field work, and reimbursement
structure.critical_dependency: OEM and distributor participation with serial, warranty-rule, RMA, shipment, and reimbursement data

thesis: Create a neutral claim-administration layer between PV/storage OEMs, distributors, and installers. It binds serial number, warranty entitlement, commissioning and invoice evidence, telemetry-led diagnosis, RMA approval, site labor, replacement shipment, and reimbursement into one case. OEMs retain adjudication authority; the network earns on a completed claim and enterprise workflow subscription, then compounds a permissioned defect and repair benchmark across brands.
title: Multi-Brand Renewable Warranty Claim Clearing Network
uncertainties: Claim volume, processing cost, and rejection rate in the target region are unknown.
It is unclear whether an OEM, distributor, or large installer is the best initial payer.
OEM APIs and rights to normalize warranty rules are untested.
The amount of genuinely reusable cross-brand data may be limited by confidentiality.
